articles.title: Thiruparankundram: 2,000 Years on One Hill
articles.description: A visual historical timeline of the layered Jain, Hindu and Islamic heritage of Thiruparankundram, Madurai, including archaeological evidence, literature, inscriptions, legal records and the Deepathoon dispute.

articles.title: How did a Harappan city store water in one of India's driest landscapes?
articles.description: At Dholavira in Gujarat's Kutch, seasonal streams, reservoirs, check dams and stone channels helped a Harappan city manage scarce water for centuries.
articles.imageAlt: Stone-built reservoir at the Dholavira Harappan site

articles.title: India extracts 60% of its groundwater. Rajasthan extracts 133% of its annual recharge.
articles.description: India's 2025 groundwater assessment shows a national extraction stage of 60.63%. Rajasthan's annual extraction is about 133% of annual recharge, with 213 of 302 blocks over-exploited.
articles.imageAlt: Agricultural fields and farm pond in Rajasthan

articles.title: The Aravallis are more than hills. The Supreme Court's definition deadline is now days away.
articles.description: The Supreme Court has asked an expert panel to report by 30 November 2026 on how the Aravalli Hills and Ranges should be defined. Here's why the boundary matters.
articles.imageAlt: Green ridgelines of the Aravalli landscape in Rajasthan

articles.title: A 15-year-old hit 28 sixes. Now Indian cricket has a different problem.
articles.description: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 204 off 53 balls for India A broke List A records. The numbers, the Yuvraj Singh conversation, his setbacks and the question facing Indian cricket.

articles.title: Was Kashmir Once a Giant Lake? The Satisar Legend & the Evidence
articles.description: A story-led journey through Kashmir's Satisar legend, the valley's geological past and the people who lived at Burzahom around 5,000 years ago.

articles.title: The Burial That Left Archaeologists With More Questions
articles.description: A Neolithic site in Kashmir produced human burials, evidence of skull surgery and a remarkable burial of five wild dogs. What can the finds really tell us?

articles.title: The People Who Built Their Homes Underground
articles.description: Inside Burzahom, where Neolithic families dug homes into the earth, made tools from bone and stone, and adapted to Kashmir's harsh seasons.

articles.title: When Giant Stones Rose in Kashmir
articles.description: After the pit-dwelling world of Burzahom, huge standing stones marked a new chapter. Explore Kashmir's megalithic remains and evidence of wider connections.

articles.title: The Man Who Tried to Record Kashmir's Entire Past
articles.description: In the 12th century, Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini, a chronicle of Kashmir's kings. Discover his sources, his method and where legend meets history.

articles.title: Who Were the Nagas of Ancient Kashmir?
articles.description: Were Kashmir's Nagas serpents, human communities or sacred guardians? Follow the Nilamata Purana, ancient place traditions and what scholars can—and cannot—say.

articles.title: When Ashoka's World Reached Kashmir
articles.description: Kashmir's traditions connect Ashoka with Srinagari and Buddhism. Explore the story while separating later chronicles, Buddhist memory and archaeological evidence.

articles.title: Kanishka, Buddhist Scholars and the Kashmir Connection
articles.description: The Kushan age connected Kashmir to a vast world of trade and ideas. Explore Kanishka, Buddhist learning and the debated Fourth Buddhist Council.

articles.title: The King Who Built a Sun Temple in the Mountains
articles.description: Lalitaditya, the Karkota dynasty and Martand Sun Temple: the story behind one of Kashmir's most extraordinary surviving monuments.

articles.title: Kashmir's Thinker Who Changed the Way India Understood Consciousness
articles.description: Meet Abhinavagupta, the Kashmir philosopher whose work shaped Shaiva philosophy, aesthetics, theatre and the study of consciousness.

articles.title: India's Waste Rules Changed in 2026. Will Cities Change With Them?
articles.description: A practical explainer on India's Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and what they mean for households, bulk generators and local bodies.

articles.title: Water Scarcity Is Not Just About Rainfall. It Is About the Whole System
articles.description: Rainfall matters, but storage, groundwater, demand, leakage, pollution and access determine whether water reaches people.

articles.title: After the Bin: Where Does a City's Waste Actually Go?
articles.description: Follow household waste from collection to sorting, recycling, processing and disposal—and see where the system can fail.

articles.title: Jantar Mantar Jaipur: When Astronomy Became Architecture
articles.description: Explore how Sawai Jai Singh II turned astronomical observation into monumental instruments at Jaipur's Jantar Mantar, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

articles.title: Why Do Villages Become Abandoned? The Forces That Empty a Place
articles.description: From jobs and migration to water stress, conflict and changing transport, village abandonment rarely has one cause.

articles.title: Why Do Lakes Turn Bright Green? The Science Behind an Algal Bloom
articles.description: A lake turning green can be a sign of algae or cyanobacteria multiplying rapidly. Understand nutrients, sunlight, water movement and the warning signs that matter.

articles.title: Why Do Human Societies Create Gods, Myths and Origin Stories?
articles.description: Myths help communities explain origins, express values, remember places and make sense of uncertainty. Their meanings vary across cultures.
